newsitem.title: FRANCE: French farmers want EU to renegotiate Blair House.
newsitem.headline: French farmers want EU to renegotiate Blair House.

text.p: French oilseed producers on Monday urged the European Commission to renegotiate the 1992 Blair House pact.

Jean-Claude Sabin, president of French oilseeds and protein federation FOP, said he opposed the idea that planned EU reforms which include a single area aid for both oilseeds and cereals would make the Blair House deal disappear.
"We must find a solution that combines a basic aid for all areas and a specific aid for oilseeds. We know this will imply area limitations but this must be renegotiated," Sabin told Reuters.
Earlier Commission agriculture director-general Guy Legras said that the 1992 Blair House pact between the United States and European Union would be sidelined by the new CAP reform.
"Legras is making a mistake. He must renegotiate Blair House," Sabin said.
Sabin said the EU was wrong in scrapping aids to oilseed producers ahead of new trade talks from 1999 because this would weaken its bargaining power.

Under EU farm reforms known as Agenda 2000 the European Commission has proposed a single area aid payment of 66 Ecus a tonne for both oilseeds and cereals. This compares with previous levels of 94 Ecus for oilseeds and 54.35 Ecus for cereals.
Oilseeds producers fear a single area aid payment will lead farmers to plant less oilseeds and lower production.
